items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source (Arbitrary Code Execution)
items.summary: This update resolves a critical vulnerability (CVSS 10.0) in the webhooks component that can lead to arbitrary code execution without authentication or user interaction. It affects all supported 2.4.x lines of Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source (Unrestricted Upload of Dangerous File Type)
items.summary: A critical vulnerability (CVSS 9.6) allows attackers to upload malicious files to the server, potentially leading to remote code execution. This issue is part of the APSB26-73 security update for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source.

items.title: Adobe Commerce DOS Vulnerability
items.summary: This denial-of-service vulnerability in Adobe Commerce is caused by a dependency on a vulnerable third-party component. Successful exploitation can crash the application, disrupting storefront and administrative availability.

items.title: Adobe Commerce Auth Bypass Vulnerability
items.summary: An Incorrect Authorization vulnerability (CWE-863) in Adobe Commerce allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to bypass security checks and gain unauthorized write access. This flaw has a CVSS 3.1 base score of 7.5.

items.id: PolyShell (CVE not explicitly stated in source, but linked to Magento 2.4.9 fix)
items.title: PolyShell: unrestricted file upload in Magento and Adobe Commerce
items.summary: Sansec discovered a critical flaw in Magento's REST API that enables unauthenticated attackers to upload executable files to any store. The attack uses a polyglot to bypass validation, and while Magento 2.4.9 contains a fix, older supported versions remain vulnerable.

items.title: Critical Security Update: Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This critical security update addresses multiple vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to bypass security controls, gain escalated privileges, and execute unauthorized malicious code. Adobe recommends applying the patches as quickly as possible.
